info.title: OpenProtein
info.description:
OpenProtein API helps you engineer better proteins 🚀

# Getting Started

Here's a quick overview of our authentication and jobs system, as well as some
of our APIs.

## Navigating the Job System

Our endpoints follow an asynchronous POST and GET framework. Once you initiate
a task via our POST endpoints, the system schedules the job. This means that
even for tasks that may take a while to complete, your request will return
immediately.

The POST response will contain a job ID (`job_id`) in its response json. This
job ID is a unique identifier that allows you to track your job. You can use
this same job ID with our GET endpoints to monitor the progress of your task.
Please note that only **you** can access your jobs, a different user cannot
access your jobs even with your specific job ID.

Whilst your job is underway, the API will indicate the status as `PENDING`.
Once the job has concluded (`SUCCESS`), you can retrieve your results by
invoking the same endpoint using your job ID in the payload (see specific
endpoint details for more guidance).
The `/api/v1/jobs/JOB_ID` endpoint is at your disposal to check the status of
a job before obtaining all the results.

This design ensures that long-running tasks don't keep you waiting, and ensures
you can always get the results of a job back at a later date.

Remember, your job ID is both unique and crucial for fetching the results of
your task. So, ensure to keep a note of it when you initiate a task.

# Endpoints

## Login

Endpoints to login from your IDE. Here's a brief user-guide:

### Steps to Log in

#### On this Page

You can log in directly on this page using the `Authorize` button. This action
will let you browse the API documentation and execute test queries directly in
your browser.


## Jobs

Endpoints to track job status for asynchronous jobs.

Use these to verify the status (PENDING, RUNNING, SUCCESS) of your jobs and
view basic metadata (e.g., job creation date).

## Align

Endpoints to perform multiple sequence alignment (MSA) workflows. See the [User Guide](https://docs.openprotein.ai/poet-defining-prompts-page.html).

You can create a multiple sequence alignment from a seed sequence, upload a
custom MSA, or even upload your own prompt for use with `PoET` and `Fold`
endpoints!


## Assaydata

Endpoints to upload your dataset to OpenProtein's engineering platform for
`train`, `predict` and `evaluate` tasks. See the
[User Guide](https://docs.openprotein.ai/dataset-page.html).

Format your data as 2 column CSV:
* The full sequence of each variant (mutation codes are also accepted)
* 1+ columns with your measured properties (missing values are acceptable)

## Libraries

Endpoints to fetch of all your designed OpenProtein sequence variants. This
enables you to reference previously created variants easily.

post.description:
Upload a pre-made prompt and bypass all MSA and Sampling criteria steps.

The number of replicates is determined by the number of prompts         included in the upload.
Each individual prompt in the file should be seperated with `<END_PROMPT>` flags.

Currently supports CSV and Fa formats.
For CSV we expect a headerless upload including either:

    * a 2 column file: Names, Sequences
    * a 1 column file: Sequences

---

Args: 

    - prompt_file (File): csv or fa file to use as prompt as-is

Raises: 

    - HTTPException (40X): If job can not be created


Returns: 

    - Job: submitted Job details
---

Creates a prompt from an existing MSA created from /align/msa endpoint.

Filtering criteria (e.g. homology_level) are applied to the MSA to create a prompt        for use downstream use in poet applications.

You can and should view the results of this step with `/align/inputs msa_type='PROMPT'` before proceeding to poet endpoints.

---

Args: 

    - msa_id (str): A job_id from POST /aign/msa results.
    - max_msa_sequences (int): maximum number of sequences to sample from MSA.
        Exclusive with max_msa_tokens.
    - max_msa_tokens (int): maximum number of combined residues to sample from MSA.
        Exclusive with max_msa_sequences.
    - homology_level (float): The level of sequence identity used for sampling
        non-redundant sequences from the MSA (neighbors sampling only).
        For example, a homology level of 0.8 means that a sequence is considered to
        belong to the same redundant group as other sequences to which it has >=80% identity.
    - seed (int): seed for random sampling
    - max_similarity (float): the max allowed similarity between the seed
        and subsequent sequences from the MSA.
    - min_similarity (float): the min allowed similarity between the seed
        and subsequent sequences from the MSA.
    - force_include_first (bool): whether to always include the seed (first)
        sequence from the MSA
    - msa_method (str): one of the following sampling strategies:
        - Top: Select sequences in the order in which they occur in the MSA.
        - Random: Sample sequences randomly without replacement from the MSA.
        - Neighbors (reccomended): Sample more diverse, less redundant sequences
            from the MSA by sampling each sequence with weight inversely
            proportional to its number of homologs in the MSA.
            see homology_level for finer control of this strategy.
    - replicates: the number of unique prompts to create.
        Used to ensemble models downstream.

Raises: 

    - HTTPException (40X): If job can not be created

Returns: 

    - Job: submitted Job details
---

**Deprecated.** For seed-based MSA generation use `POST /align/search/mmseqs2/msa`;
to store a ready-made MSA use `POST /api/v1/data/msa`. Retained for backward
compatibility until callers migrate.

Create a multiple sequence alignment (MSA).

Either upload a seed sequence (is_seed = True) to have ColabFold generate an MSA,         or upload an entire, pre-made MSA directly (is_seed = False).

For a complex, upload a single MSA in ColabFold combined-a3m form: chains joined         with `:`, or the `#<lengths>       <cardinalities>` header.

File Uploads:
We currently support CSV, Fasta / a3m formats.
For CSV we expect a headerless upload including either:

    * a 2 column file: Names, Sequences
    * a 1 column file: Sequences

Args: 

    - msa_file (File): CSV or Fa/a3m (see above)
    - is_seed (bool): whether to use the first sequence as a seed for the MSA.
        Note that if True, everything past the first sequence is discarded.

Raises: 

    - HTTPException (40X): If job can not be created

Returns: 

    - Job: submitted Job details
---

post.description:
Annotate one or more antibody sequences and stream the result back as a CSV.

The endpoint accepts either an inline list of antibody amino-acid
sequences (`sequences`) or a reference to an existing assay
(`assay_id`). Exactly one of those two fields must be supplied. Each
input sequence may be a single chain (heavy or light) or a paired
heavy/light pair joined by a single `:` (e.g.
`EVQLVES...:DIQMTQS...`). Sequences containing the `(GGGGS)x3`
linker are normalised to colon-paired form before annotation.

For each input sequence the service:

1. Numbers the sequence according to the chosen `scheme` (IMGT,
   Kabat, Chothia, or AHo) and chosen CDR definition.
2. Determines the chain type (`H`, `K`, or `L`) and assigns the
   best-matching V and J germline genes from the requested species'
   germline database.
3. Computes the number of mutations, substitutions, insertions, and
   deletions relative to the assigned germline. Mutation metrics are
   always computed in IMGT numbering over the V region (IMGT
   positions <= 104), independent of the chosen `scheme`, so that
   the counts are directly comparable across schemes.

### Output format

The response is a `text/csv` stream consisting of:

1. A single metadata comment line beginning with `# ` and containing
   a JSON object of scheme-specific metadata: region boundaries plus
   the position-ordering information needed to reconstruct
   alignments from the `numbering` labels. See the "Metadata
   comment" section below for the fields.
2. A header row listing the columns:
   `chain_type,numbering,v_gene,j_gene,n_mutations,n_substitutions,n_insertions,n_deletions,error`.
3. One data row per input sequence, in input order.

Column meanings:

| Column | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `chain_type` | `H` (heavy), `K` (kappa light), or `L` (lambda light). For paired sequences, the two chain-type letters are concatenated with no separator, in input order (e.g. `HK`, `HL`, `KH`, `LH`). |
| `numbering` | Comma-separated list of position labels in the chosen scheme, with one entry per residue of the input sequence. Each label is the residue number with an optional insertion letter appended (e.g. `35`, `35A`, `100A`). Residues that the scheme could not number (only ever at the sequence ends) appear as `?`. Position numbers may not be contiguous: gaps indicate residues that the scheme considers deleted relative to its canonical numbering, and inserted residues take the next free insertion letter. For paired sequences, the heavy and light numbering strings are joined with `:`. See the "Numbering examples" section below. |
| `v_gene` | Best-matching V germline gene call. |
| `j_gene` | Best-matching J germline gene call. |
| `n_mutations` | Total residues differing from the assigned germline (`n_substitutions + n_insertions + n_deletions`), measured over the IMGT V region (positions <= 104). |
| `n_substitutions` | Substitutions relative to germline, measured over the IMGT V region. |
| `n_insertions` | Insertions relative to germline, measured over the IMGT V region. |
| `n_deletions` | Deletions relative to germline, measured over the IMGT V region. |
| `error` | Empty on success; on failure, a JSON object with `sequence_index`, `sequence`, and `error`. |

### Error modes

The `error_mode` field controls per-sequence error handling:

- `row` (default): each failing sequence emits a row with empty
  annotation columns and a populated `error` field; processing
  continues for the remaining sequences. The CSV is streamed
  progressively as rows become available.
- `strict`: any sequence that fails to annotate aborts the request
  with a `400` response; on success, the response is always a
  complete CSV.

When `assay_id` is supplied, `error_mode` must be `row`.

### Numbering scheme and CDR definition

The `scheme` field selects the numbering convention applied to each
chain. For `imgt`, `chothia`, and `kabat` the CDR boundaries default
to the scheme's native definition; you may override them by setting
`cdr_definition`. The `aho` scheme does not define CDR boundaries on
its own, so `cdr_definition` is **required** when `scheme="aho"` and
must be one of `imgt`, `chothia`, `kabat`, or `north`.

### Numbering examples

Basic single chain (one label per input residue):

```
1,2,3,...,113
```

Paired heavy/light, the two chains' label lists joined with `:`:

```
1,2,...,113:1,2,...,107
```

Input residues that the scheme could not number, marked `?` (one
`?` per unnumbered residue; only ever appears at the sequence
ends):

```
?,?,1,2,3,...,113
```

### Metadata comment

The metadata comment line on the first row of the CSV is a single
JSON object with the following fields:

- `region_number_ranges`: per chain type (`H`, `K`, `L`), the
  start/end residue numbers of each region (`FR1`, `CDR1`, `FR2`,
  `CDR2`, `FR3`, `CDR3`, `FR4`).
- `reverse_insertion_letter_numbers`: residue positions whose
  insertion-letter ordering is reversed for the chosen scheme (e.g.
  IMGT positions 33, 61, and 112).
- `vernier_numbers`: present only when `scheme="kabat"`; per chain
  type, the residue numbers that are part of the Vernier zone.

200.description: Streaming CSV containing one row per input sequence, prefixed by a metadata comment line and a header row. See the endpoint description for column meanings.

400.description: Invalid request. Returned when the payload fails validation (e.g. neither or both of `sequences` and `assay_id` provided, `scheme="aho"` without `cdr_definition`, `assay_id` combined with `error_mode="strict"`, or, under `error_mode="strict"`, when a sequence cannot be annotated).

401.description: Bad or expired token. The token is missing, revoked, or has expired; re-authenticate with credentials.

403.description: The authenticated user is not permitted to access the referenced assay.

422.description: Unexpected request format. The submitted body could not be parsed against the request schema. Double-check field names, types, and constraints.

get.description:
Get metadata for MSA and prompts.

MSA and prompts are created by align/msa & align/prompt or align/upload_prompt.

Set replicate to None to fetch all available replicates.

---
Args: 

    - job_id (str): job_id
    - msa_type (MSAType): One of the following:
        - RAW: user uploaded file
        - GENERATED: MSA from ColabFold (or User upload)
        - PROMPT: returns the sub-sample of MSA used for poet (if available)
    - replicate (int): the replicate to return, only applied to msa_type=PROMPT.

Raises: 

    - HTTPException (40X): If job can not be found

Returns:
    - List(jsons)
---

AlignJob.title: AlignJob
AlignJob.description: Properties returned about job via API.

sequences.title: Sequences
sequences.description: List of antibody amino-acid sequences to annotate, in the order the results should appear in the response CSV. Mutually exclusive with `assay_id`.

assay_id.title: Assay ID
assay_id.description: ID of an assay whose sequences should be annotated. Mutually exclusive with `sequences`; when set, `error_mode` must be `row`.

scheme.title: Numbering scheme
scheme.description:
Antibody numbering scheme.

- `imgt`: IMGT unique numbering.
- `chothia`: Chothia numbering.
- `kabat`: Kabat numbering.
- `aho`: AHo numbering. Requires `cdr_definition` to be set.

cdr_definition.title: CDR definition
cdr_definition.description: CDR boundary definition used when reporting region ranges. Optional for `imgt`, `chothia`, and `kabat` (which fall back to their native CDR boundaries); **required** when `scheme` is `aho`.

allowed_species.title: Allowed species
allowed_species.description: Species germline database used for V/J gene assignment.

error_mode.title: Error mode
error_mode.description:
How errors on individual sequences are handled.

- `row`: per-sequence errors land in the `error` column; processing continues. Required when `assay_id` is used.
- `strict`: any sequence that fails to annotate aborts the request with a `400`.
